ProjectSpecification__Description: Project specification notes for the TrueVision drawings. Groups hold notes in order; a note’s code is its group’s prefix and its place in the group (GN01, EE02), so the order is the truth and Note__Code is written for readers and recomputed on every load. Specification bubbles on the Layout Editor sheets link to notes by Note__Id. General groups are listed on every sheet’s notes margin, after the notes that sheet’s bubbles link to. LastIdNumber only ever goes up, so no id is used twice.

Group__Notes.Note__Body: Drawings describe the proposed development for planning assessment. They are not construction drawings or a complete Building Regulations specification. Obtain coordinated construction details, structural calculations and Building Control approval before relevant work starts. Refer discrepancies to Noble Architecture before proceeding.

Prepared from client-supplied photographs and measurements; Noble Architecture has not undertaken a measured site survey. Verify dimensions, levels, boundaries and existing construction on site before design, ordering or setting out. Use stated dimensions; do not scale for construction. Report discrepancies before work proceeds.

Single-storey rear extension projecting 3,150 mm beyond the rear wall of the original dwellinghouse. Projection is measured from the base of the rear wall of the original house to the outer edge of the wall of the extension, not including any guttering or barge boards. Reference: MHCLG, Permitted development rights for householders: Technical Guidance (September 2019), page 18.

Extension width 9,230 mm within an existing rear elevation of 10,030 mm. The extension does not extend beyond any wall forming a side elevation of the original dwellinghouse, so the side-extension limits at Class A.1(j) are not engaged. Reference: MHCLG, Permitted development rights for householders: Technical Guidance (September 2019), page 22.

Extension eaves height 2,600 mm, measured from the planning ground datum (PD05) at the base of the external wall of the extension to the point where that wall, projected upwards, meets the upper surface of the flat roof. The parapet wall and any overhang are excluded. Eaves of the existing dwellinghouse on the same elevation: 2,650 mm. The extension eaves therefore sits 50 mm below the eaves of the existing dwellinghouse and does not exceed it, satisfying Class A.1(d). Basis of measurement: PD06, PD07 and PD08.

Top of parapet 2,880 mm above the planning ground datum (PD05). The parapet is excluded from eaves height (PD06, PD07) but is counted in the overall height of the enlarged part: "when calculating the height of the enlarged part of the house, this measurement should be at the highest part of the enlargement and may include any protrusions above the roof such as parapet walls etc". At 2,880 mm the enlarged part is below the 4 m limit for a single-storey rear extension at Class A.1(f)(ii) and below the height of the highest part of the roof of the existing dwellinghouse required by Class A.1(c). Reference: MHCLG, Permitted development rights for householders: Technical Guidance (September 2019), pages 11 and 17.

Class A.1(d): development is not permitted if "the height of the eaves of the part of the dwellinghouse enlarged, improved or altered would exceed the height of the eaves of the existing dwellinghouse". The guidance defines the measurement: "For the purpose of measuring height, the eaves of a house are the point where the lowest point of a roof slope, or a flat roof, meets the outside wall. The height of the eaves will be measured from the ground level at the base of the external wall of the extension to the point where the external wall would meet (if projected upwards) the upper surface of the roof slope. Parapet walls and overhanging parts of eaves should not be included in any calculation of eaves height." Reference: MHCLG, Permitted development rights for householders: Technical Guidance (September 2019), page 11.

Group__Notes.Note__Title: Eaves on a flat roof behind a parapet
Group__Notes.Note__Body: The guidance illustrates this exact arrangement, a flat roof with a parapet wall, and states: "Eaves height is measured from the ground level at the base of the outside wall to the point where that wall would meet the upper surface of the flat roof - the overhang and the parapet wall should be ignored for the purposes of measurement." The extension eaves point marked on the drawings is set accordingly, at the upper surface of the flat roof where it meets the outside wall, with the parapet disregarded. Reference: MHCLG, Permitted development rights for householders: Technical Guidance (September 2019), page 12, flat roof diagram.

Group__Notes.Note__Title: Eaves on the existing pitched roof
Group__Notes.Note__Body: The eaves of the existing dwellinghouse are taken at the same defined point on its pitched roof: "Eaves height is measured from ground level at the base of the outside wall to the point where that wall would meet the upper surface of the roof slope - the overhang should be ignored for the purposes of measurement." The host dwelling eaves point marked on the drawings is therefore taken at the upper surface of the roof slope projected to the face of the outside wall, with the gutter and overhanging eaves disregarded. Reference: MHCLG, Permitted development rights for householders: Technical Guidance (September 2019), page 12, pitched roof diagram.

Group__Notes.Note__Title: Eaves benchmark taken on this elevation
Group__Notes.Note__Body: Where the existing house has eaves of different heights the restriction is measured against the highest level of eaves on the existing house; where a house is built on sloping ground the eaves of the existing house "should be measured in terms of the elevation from which any extension of a house is to be made". The comparison shown is taken on the rear elevation from which the extension is made: existing dwellinghouse eaves 2,650 mm against extension eaves 2,600 mm. Measuring instead against the highest eaves on the existing house would raise the permitted level, so the comparison drawn is the more restrictive of the two. Reference: MHCLG, Permitted development rights for householders: Technical Guidance (September 2019), page 13.

Group__Notes.Note__Title: Eaves within 2 m of a boundary
Group__Notes.Note__Body: Class A.1(i): development is not permitted if "the enlarged part of the dwellinghouse would be within 2 metres of the boundary of the curtilage of the dwellinghouse, and the height of the eaves of the enlarged part would exceed 3 metres". The guidance confirms that "guidance on measurement of height of eaves is covered under paragraph (d) above", so the parapet is excluded from this test as well. At an eaves height of 2,600 mm the extension is 400 mm below the 3 m limit, and the limit is met whether or not any part of the extension lies within 2 m of a boundary. Reference: MHCLG, Permitted development rights for householders: Technical Guidance (September 2019), page 22.

The extension eaves is set 50 mm below the eaves of the existing dwellinghouse. That margin carries the whole of the compliance case at Class A.1(d), so the wall plate, deck and roof build-up must be set out so the upper surface of the flat roof where it meets the external wall does not rise above 2,600 mm from the planning ground datum (PD05). Confirm the existing dwellinghouse eaves height by survey before setting out; if it is found to be lower than 2,650 mm the extension roof must be lowered to match, since exceeding it removes permitted development rights.

Structural members shown are indicative. Appoint a structural engineer to inspect the existing building and design foundations, beams, lintels, posts, bearings, connections and lateral restraint. Obtain coordinated calculations and details before structural work; do not derive member sizes from these drawings.

Structural engineer to design support over the wide sliding-door opening, including bearings, padstones, supporting piers or posts and foundations. Limit deflection to the door supplier's tolerances. Coordinate head clearance, frame fixings, insulation and weathering before manufacture.

Engineer to assess retained walls, roof loads and stability before enlarging rear openings. Specify permanent support and restraint. Contractor to provide an engineered temporary support and demolition sequence; install supports before removing loadbearing construction. Do not assume existing lintels or foundations are adequate.

Confirm ground conditions, trees, drains and adjacent foundations before foundation design. Do not reuse conservatory foundations without the engineer's verification. Design roof joists and rooflight trimmers for the complete warm-roof build-up, parapets and imposed loads; coordinate openings before fabrication.

Existing house: mixed buff facing brickwork above a blue engineering-brick plinth to DPC level. Retain outside the indicated alterations; make good disturbed areas with matching bricks and mortar. Confirm brick types and DPC level on site.

Existing brown small-format tiles to pitched roof; clay or concrete composition to be confirmed on site. Retain roof covering outside the works. Match replacement tiles where disturbed and weather extension abutments without obstructing existing roof ventilation.

Existing windows and external doors comprise mixed white and brown frames, including uPVC, with varied glazing patterns. Retain except where removal or replacement is indicated. Confirm frame materials, opening arrangements and finishes on site.

Existing felt-covered flat roof over the WC is reported to be at the end of its service life. Remove with the WC structure; inspect and make good retained abutments. Do not incorporate the existing covering into the new roof.

Remove existing conservatory and adjoining flat-roof WC, approximately 3,100 mm projection x 4,350 mm overall width. Isolate services and seal redundant drain connections. Protect retained walls and roof; make good exposed junctions. Confirm demolition extent and any retained foundations on site.

Where retained facing brickwork is disturbed, match the existing brick colour, size, bond, mortar colour and joint profile. Agree a sample before work. New extension wall finishes are specified in WF01-WF03.
Exterior walls to match the existing brickwork of the existing property, mortar joints to be pointed and coloured the same as the existing house. All bricks to be the same tone, texture, and quality.

Blue engineering-brick plinth up to DPC, matching the original house in colour, size, bond and pointing. Coordinate DPC with the floor membrane and external levels; maintain 150 mm clearance above finished ground except at separately detailed accessible thresholds.

Warm-roof construction behind a parapet, with insulation above the structural deck and a continuous vapour control layer below the insulation. Coordinate thermal performance, condensation control, waterproofing and abutments in the construction details. Form falls to outlets within the stated height envelope.

Parapet conceals the warm-roof edge; coping level to PD04. Provide weathered copings with drips, secure fixings and sealed joints; turn roof waterproofing up the inner face beneath the coping system. Maintain insulation continuity at the roof edge.

Form positive falls to sized roof outlets and rainwater pipes. Provide accessible outlets and an emergency overflow to the parapet-enclosed roof. Confirm discharge route and capacity before construction; keep all roof drainage within the site and clear of door thresholds.

Large glazed sliding doors to the east, garden-facing elevation. Frame material, colour, panel arrangement and opening direction to be confirmed. Coordinate structural opening and deflection tolerances with the supplier. Provide safety glazing, weather seals and a drained threshold; confirm thermal performance and ventilation in the construction specification.

New uPVC window to the bedroom on the east, garden-facing elevation. Colour and opening arrangement to be agreed. Coordinate glazing, ventilation and any required escape opening with the Building Regulations design; confirm clear opening dimensions and sill height before ordering.
